summary.name: 法脉 LawPulse
summary.one_liner: A local-first desktop legal research tool for Chinese lawyers that offers offline search of 56,182 statute articles, per-article notes, case folders, and optional AI contract review and drafting.
use_cases: Searching Chinese statutes and case law offline
Taking notes and highlights on individual law articles
Reviewing a contract with AI and checking cited articles against the local library
Drafting legal documents from case folder material
Redacting client names and contact details before sending text to a cloud AI model
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a Chinese-law research workbench where 1,513 current laws, administrative regulations and judicial interpretations (56,182 articles) are searchable offline, drawn from the national legal regulations database; it also includes 278 guiding cases and 445 gazette cases. Users can do full-text search via a ⌘K box, keep notes and highlights per article, organize work into case folders, and export to Word/PDF. Paid-tier features include AI Q&A that cites local sources, contract review that checks cited articles against the local library, and document drafting. The page states the app has no relay server for user materials; when cloud AI is used, submitted content goes to the chosen model provider. It also describes a built-in PII redaction feature before cloud AI calls.
notable: Offline statute library with clickable citation verification in AI contract review
No relay server; notes and contracts stay local, with redaction before cloud AI calls
Free core features (search, notes, case folders, export) with no account needed
caveats: Local and departmental regulations are not yet included; users must import them, and regional libraries are still in preparation
AI features, contract review, and live law updates are paid (monthly, annual, or one-time purchase) and require internet; AI model costs are billed separately by the provider
Only laws downloaded in advance work offline; there is no cloud sync and data files are not encrypted by default
